extracted.intended_audience: research scientists applying for EMBO | EuropaBio Fellowships (short research exchanges between laboratories)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting applications for EMBO | EuropaBio Fellowships to fund short (7 days) to medium (up to 6 months) research visits between laboratories in eligible EMBC/associate/cooperating countries. Covers eligibility, application materials, proposal format, selection criteria, reporting and administrative requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application deadline and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are accepted from 1 September 2017 until 31 December 2017. Decisions will be communicated by 31 March 2018. Awarded research visits must begin in 2018.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines are firm; applicants should ensure proposed visits fall within the required timing. (Original text gives specific 2017/2018 dates.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications from outside EMBC Member States, Associated Member States or Cooperation Partners will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMBC Member states and Associate/Cooperating partners are listed (e.g., Austria, Belgium, India, Singapore, Taiwan etc.). Exchanges between two laboratories within the same country are not awarded; international laboratories that are extraterritorial (e.g., EMBL) are permitted as hosts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and duration of fellowship
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships support research visits of one week (seven days) up to six months (180 days) between laboratories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowships are intended for joint research work rather than consultations, preferably to establish new scientific relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities and projects not eligible
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for fellowships to attend courses, workshops, or symposia will not be considered; applications to develop new products or procedures in industrial research laboratories or for commercial purposes will not be considered; exclusive training in a technique (without being part of a wider research project) will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects with industrial/commercial aims or purely training/attendance purposes are ineligible. Short (one- or two-day) visits or seminar invitations are also not counted as parallel exchanges but are not intended uses of the fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant research experience requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must be an active research scientist at any stage in their career with at least one year of research experience at PhD student level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a minimum eligibility threshold; include evidence of research experience in CV/present-work synopsis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reapplication and prior EMBO fellowship rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Holding a previous EMBO Short or Long-Term Fellowship does not preclude further applications for a new project in a different laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reapplication is possible only twelve months after the end of the previous Short-Term Fellowship or, in the case of unsuccessful applicants, twelve months after the date of application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions regarding host lab and prior relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications to work with former PhD or postdoc supervisors or to work in laboratories previously visited will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications to visit laboratories in the context of an already existing long-term collaboration or involving previous exchanges of scientists have low priority for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return-to-home requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: On completion of the fellowship applicants must return to their home laboratory for at least six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A signed letter from the home institution after this period is required as proof; applicants must provide this certification after the fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: No parallel exchanges allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not possible to apply for an EMBO | EuropaBio Fellowship if other, parallel exchanges are planned to take place between the home and the host laboratories during the planned fellowship duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short (one- or two-day) visits or seminar invitations are not considered in this category. Applicants should declare planned exchanges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of additional funding
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant has secured additional funds or grants from other institutions to support the proposed visit, the applicant must notify the EMBO Fellowship Office immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose concurrent funding sources during application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application language and submission medium
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications must be written in English and are accepted via the EMBO online application system; hard copies will not be processed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All relevant documents (application form, reference letters, host acceptance) must be submitted electronically through the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants must register for ORCID digital identifiers (iDs) to ensure unambiguous name assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide ORCID ID in the application; a link to register (https://orcid.org/register) is given for applicants without an ID.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of reference requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must provide the names and contact details of two referees (who are not from the host institute) who will submit confidential letters of reference online. One referee must be the current supervisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant is already an independent researcher, only one reference letter from a legal representative of the home institution (Dean, Director etc.) is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host institute acceptance form requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must provide the name and contact details of their host supervisor, and the host supervisor must submit an acceptance form online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should coordinate the application with the receiving institute; the host acceptance form is required for a complete application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness and acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is only complete once both reference letters (if applicable) and the host institute acceptance form have been received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receipt of submitted applications will be acknowledged via email and an EMBO | EuropaBio Fellowship reference (ASTF) number will be assigned upon submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research proposal length and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal is subdivided into a 250-word summary of the proposed activity and biological significance, plus the research proposal itself, which must not exceed 1500 words (excluding references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The research proposal should explain the background and contain a detailed outline of the work to be performed at the host institute. No figures or tables may be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: References format requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: References in the research proposal should include the complete list of authors followed by the title of the paper, year, journal or preprint server name and details on volume, page numbers, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified bibliographic completeness; preprints (e.g., arXiv, bioRxiv, PeerJ) are acceptable in evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical and research integrity compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: All research activities supported must be in compliance with fundamental ethical and research integrity principles (e.g., the Belmont Report and the Singapore Statement on Research Integrity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These refer to questions relevant to use of human materials (including human embryonic stem cells), use of animal models, and other ethical issues; applicants may be asked to provide evidence that planned research conforms to relevant host/home regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present work synopsis and future career plans
rubrics_metrics.description: The synopsis of work performed at the home institute should allow the reader to appreciate the applicant’s past experience and its relevance to the proposed research topic and must clearly communicate career plans for the period following the Fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be brief and concise; emphasize relevance of past experience to the proposed exchange and intended career trajectory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication list rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must indicate their three (or fewer) most important publications — the three primary research papers that in their view provided the most important and original contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must NOT include journal impact factor (EMBO is a signatory of DORA). Papers uploaded to preprint servers will be taken into consideration. Papers submitted or in preparation, not yet accessible to the community, will not be considered and must not be included. Publication updates after application will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criterion: Quality of the project
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are judged on the quality of the project to be developed in the host laboratory (novelty, feasibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how novel the proposed work is and whether the proposed plan is feasible within the visit duration and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criterion: Suitability of the host laboratory
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are judged on the suitability of the host laboratory for the proposed work and previous interactions with the home laboratory; consider whether the topic is covered in sufficient depth and breadth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the host can provide the necessary expertise, infrastructure or complementary skills to accomplish the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criterion: Value of the exchange for the laboratories involved
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are judged on the value of the exchange for the laboratories (expertise or technology transfer, collaboration, co-publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider mutual benefit, capacity building, and potential for sustained collaboration beyond the visit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criterion: CV and research experience of candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are judged on the CV of the candidate, and in particular research experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate past accomplishments, relevant skills, and ability to execute the proposed project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits and funding coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The fellowships contribute towards travel costs and subsistence of the fellow but not of any dependents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The subsistence rate depends on the country being visited; the fellowship does not cover dependent costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final report requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: At the end of their fellowship, fellows must submit a final report within 6 months of completing the research visit. The report should be about two pages and summarize the results and possible plans for further work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report may include diagrams, charts or illustrations. Upon receipt the Fellowship Office will send a certificate stating start date, duration, place, Fellowship number and project title. The report should be sent to fellowships@embo.org and must include the fellowship number and current address.
